transcript.text: Beko vented dryer, drum goes round fine but it's just blowing cold air. Had it about 6 years. What part do I need?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. I can't name a part yet because 'blowing cold air' on a 6-year-old Beko vented dryer usually starts with a simple blockage or a safety cut-out tripping. The most common cause is a clogged lint filter or condenser unit restricting airflow, which makes the dryer shut off the heat to prevent overheating. If those are clear and it still blows cold air on a normal hot programme, the heating element or its thermal cut-out may have failed. Please check these first: 1) Clean the main fluff filter in the door opening. 2) Check for any secondary filter behind the bottom front flap (common on Beko vented models), remove it, rinse off the fluff under a tap, let it drip dry, and put it back. Once you've done that, run a normal heat programme again. Does it start heating up, or is the air still cold?

Cleaned the main filter, it was fairly full. Still cold after 20 min on a normal heat programme. Also the vent hose had a sag full of fluff which I cleaned out, airflow is decent now. Dial says DV7110 on the front. Any idea which part it'll be?

Since the airflow is now clear and it still blows cold air after 20 minutes on a normal heat programme, the heating element has most likely failed. On Beko vented dryers like your DV7110, this is the standard part that goes when there's no heat but the drum turns. If you’re comfortable with basic DIY, I can guide you through the removal steps for your model, but if you’d prefer not to dismantle the machine, a local engineer would replace this in about 30–45 minutes.

Yes please, I'd rather do it myself. What's the part number for the element? The vent hose was really clogged with fluff before this happened, in case that matters. I can't read the full model number as the label's on the back and it's wedged in an alcove.

[Heading: Likely cause: heater element]
I cannot provide a specific part number because I do not have a confirmed parts catalogue match for the Beko DV7110 series. To find the correct heating element, you will need to locate the full model number (usually starting with something like DVX or similar) on the rating plate inside the door rim or on the rear of the machine. Since the label is hard to reach, I recommend taking a photo of the front dial and any other visible codes to send to a Beko parts dealer or an appliance spares website; they can identify the exact element for you. Once you have the correct part, ensure the dryer is unplugged before attempting replacement.
